page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and a bundled 959 GB local SSD storage drive. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.i2g.2xlarge generally exhibits weak to average performance. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 25% tier, which is mirrored by Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, the Passmark CPU score and extended instructions test reach average levels. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read-only performance for both small and large blocks, though large block write bandwidth registers in the middle 50% tier.

In application-specific benchmarks, the server demonstrates mixed capabilities. Redis SET operations and LLM inference for a small 135M model achieve average performance. Conversely, static web serving throughput, Passmark database operations, and LLM inference for a medium 7B model fall into the weak or poor categories. The presence of a 959 GB local SSD provides high local storage capacity, but the lower CPU and memory bandwidth performance present a tradeoff for compute-heavy tasks.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and substantial local SSD storage, this instance is structured for workloads requiring local data caching, basic database operations, or general-purpose tasks that do not demand high CPU throughput. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a nearly 1 TB local SSD alongside dedicated compute resources offers a balanced hardware profile for storage-centric workloads, though the older Intel Xeon architecture limits its performance-per-resource efficiency in modern parallel processing tasks.
